question_text: Where must you particularly reckon with dirt on the roadway and therefore danger of skidding?

options.text: Near construction sites
At junctions with farm tracks
At innercity crossroads

correct_answers.text: Near construction sites
At junctions with farm tracks

comment: At junctions of dirt roads and at construction sites, the roadway is likely to be heavily soiled with soil, clay and dirt. Vehicles coming from there bring the dirt onto the road with the tread grooves of their tyres. In wet conditions, this means an increased risk of slipping.

question_text: Why must the safe distance maintained be much greater on a wet roadway than on a dry roadway?

options.text: The contact between the tyres and the roadway deteriorates
Wheel-spray can impair visibility
Braking distances are greater

correct_answers.text: The contact between the tyres and the roadway deteriorates
Wheel-spray can impair visibility
Braking distances are greater

comment: On wet roads, the adhesion between the tyre and the road is poorer due to the water film. As a result, the braking distance is considerably longer. In addition, the spray from the car in front worsens visibility. The same applies to rainy weather.

question_text: Where must you especially reckon with ice on the roadway?

options.text: On bridges
On stretches of road running through forest
On frequently used stretches of road

correct_answers.text: On bridges
On stretches of road running through forest

comment: You must expect increased icing on the road in the following areas: in damp, shady and windy locations that favour the formation of ice on the road. These include, above all, forest locations and bridges. In forests, the cold lasts longer than in open fields. Because of the shade, moisture takes longer to evaporate here. On bridges, roadways store less heat than on the ground. Bridge roadways are therefore colder and ice up faster. The moisture of the surrounding water and the increased wind due to the unprotected location also promote icing.

question_text: What are the special conditions when driving along tree-lined avenues in the cold season?

options.text: Wet leaves as well as white frost, black ice and snowy surfaces are particularly dangerous above all on cambered roadways
White frost and black ice occur more frequently and more unexpectedly on cobbled roadways than on other roadways
Tree-lined avenues are particularly safe in winter because the treetops protect the road from snow

correct_answers.text: Wet leaves as well as white frost, black ice and snowy surfaces are particularly dangerous above all on cambered roadways
White frost and black ice occur more frequently and more unexpectedly on cobbled roadways than on other roadways

comment: The particularities of driving along avenues in the cold season result from the basic characteristics of an avenue: it is characterised by uniform rows of trees running parallel to the roadway on the right and left. The foliage of the trees creates shade on the roadway. This keeps moisture longer, which favours icing in cold weather. If the leaves fall on the roadway, it also significantly increases the risk of the vehicle slipping.

question_text: There is oil on the road. What should you do now?

options.text: I notify the fire brigade
I avoid heavy braking and abrupt steering movements
I swerve onto the left-hand side of the road

correct_answers.text: I notify the fire brigade
I avoid heavy braking and abrupt steering movements

comment: If there is oil on the road, avoid jerky steering and heavy braking; there is a risk of slipping. Provided other road users are not endangered, you can move to the left lane. Notify the fire brigade so that the oil can be bound.

question_text: What must you be prepared for here?

options.text: A vehicle coming from the right
An extended braking distance
A narrowed carriageway

correct_answers.text: A vehicle coming from the right
An extended braking distance
A narrowed carriageway

comment: Due to the weather and the corresponding conditions on the road, you have to be prepared for an extended braking distance, for a vehicle coming from the right (right before left) and for a narrowed lane.

question_text: You are driving following a heavy rain shower. What should you be aware of in this situation?

options.text: I should maintain a large safety distance between me and the vehicle ahead
It is difficult for me to detect uneven areas on the road surface
Splash water might impair my vision

correct_answers.text: I should maintain a large safety distance between me and the vehicle ahead
It is difficult for me to detect uneven areas on the road surface
Splash water might impair my vision

comment: When it rains, your view worsens. Therefore, you should enlarge your safety distance to the vehicle in front, as your braking distance is extended. Spray water can be whirled up from the vehicle in front by a wet road. This means that bumps are difficult to recognize.

question_text: Why does driving on this stretch of road require greater alertness on the part of the motorist?

options.text: The road surface is uneven and road grip varies
A tram might come from the opposite direction
Driving on the tracks is dangerous

correct_answers.text: The road surface is uneven and road grip varies
A tram might come from the opposite direction
Driving on the tracks is dangerous

comment: A tram may come towards you on the tracks, in which case the lane becomes much narrower for you. Tram tracks are also dangerous, especially when wet, because they become slippery. In addition, as there are also cobblestones, the road surface is uneven and has varying degrees of grip. This can increase the braking distance.

question_text: The road is icy for a short distance. What should you avoid here, if possible?

options.text: Accelerating
Braking
Steering wheel movements

correct_answers.text: Accelerating
Braking
Steering wheel movements

comment: On icy roads, your tyres do not grip as well as usual. Therefore, you should avoid dangerous situations, i.e. neither brake nor accelerate abruptly. You should also refrain from sudden steering movements. This could cause your vehicle to skid. Only brake and steer away from the icy surface.

question_text: While driving, how can you safely check whether the road is icy?

options.text: By carefully applying the brakes at very low speed
By jerking the steering wheel to the left and right
By rapid acceleration

correct_answers.text: By carefully applying the brakes at very low speed

comment: Test the condition of the road by braking carefully at low speed. Be sure to pay attention to the traffic behind you. Avoid jerking the steering or accelerating sharply. This could cause your vehicle to swerve and become uncontrollable.

question_text: Why must you drive with particular caution here?

options.text: Because the roadway is slippery
Because the view is obscured by the bend
Because the roadway is made narrower by the wrongly parked car

correct_answers.text: Because the roadway is slippery
Because the view is obscured by the bend
Because the roadway is made narrower by the wrongly parked car

comment: Snow makes the road slippery. There is a curve in front of you that is difficult to see and a car is parked there. You will have to pull out into the oncoming lane to drive around it. Therefore, drive extra carefully to be able to react at any time. In addition, your vehicle needs suitable tyres for good grip.

question_text: Where must you be prepared to encounter sudden fog?

options.text: Near rivers
In marshy areas
Near lakes

correct_answers.text: Near rivers
In marshy areas
Near lakes

comment: Humidity at low temperatures favours the formation of fog. Therefore, fog is more likely to occur around lakes, watercourses and rivers as well as moorland areas.

question_text: What do you do if visibility is drastically reduced by fog?

options.text: Adapt your speed in time to visibility conditions
Increase the distance from the vehicle in front
Drive up close to the vehicle in front so you can use its rear lights as an orientation point

correct_answers.text: Adapt your speed in time to visibility conditions
Increase the distance from the vehicle in front

comment: Adjust your speed and driving style to the visibility conditions. Make sure that you can stop within sight. If necessary, increase the safety distance to the vehicle in front. Fog with a visibility of 50 metres, for example, means that you may drive at a maximum of 50 km/h.

question_text: What is the right course of action here?

options.text: I brake carefully
I allow [the pedestrian] on the right to cross the road
I carefully continue driving, because there are no markings visible on the road

correct_answers.text: I brake carefully
I allow [the pedestrian] on the right to cross the road

comment: Even if the lane marking is not visible, the traffic signs show the presence of the pedestrian crossing. Brake carefully to prevent your vehicle from skidding.

question_text: Why do you have to pay particular attention here?

options.text: Because it is not clear which direction the road will take
Because the road surface is uneven
Because oncoming traffic could cut the corner

correct_answers.text: Because it is not clear which direction the road will take
Because the road surface is uneven
Because oncoming traffic could cut the corner

comment: There is a long curve in front of you, the end of which you cannot see. A fast-moving vehicle could come towards you from there and cut your lane. The road surface is also uneven and does not have an even surface. So anticipate insufficient grip and drive at an adapted speed.

question_text: You want to exit the motorway; to which must you pay particularly close attention?

options.text: The red motorbike
The yellow truck
The white van

correct_answers.text: The red motorbike

comment: In the video you see a red motorcycle on the deceleration lane. Later it is no longer visible, because it is located in the blind spot on the right side of you. Now if you also swing out on the deceleration lane, you'll cut the motorcyclist - a dangerous situation for him. Make sure that the rider passes right by you before changing lanes.

question_text: Why might taking the right turn be dangerous here?

options.text: Because I might possibly not be able to stop in time, if pedestrians are crossing the side street
Because vehicles emerging from the side street could start to skid
Because my vehicle might start to skid if I take the turn too fast

correct_answers.text: Because I might possibly not be able to stop in time, if pedestrians are crossing the side street
Because vehicles emerging from the side street could start to skid
Because my vehicle might start to skid if I take the turn too fast

comment: The winter weather makes the road slippery and increases the braking distance at the intersection. Your car or oncoming vehicles could skid or slide away uncontrollably. Therefore, reduce your speed in good time and do not brake abruptly. The road on the right is still full of snow and therefore even slicker. Watch out for pedestrians when turning. They always have priority when you turn.

question_text: You are driving on this road which is not inside a built-up area. What should you prepare yourself for?

options.text: Pedestrians using the road
The road is narrow
Pedestrians walking only off the road

correct_answers.text: Pedestrians using the road
The road is narrow

comment: On the right you will see the sign for a car park. Expect pedestrians walking away from or towards their parked cars. As the pavements are impassable due to the masses of snow, evasive pedestrians could use the roadway. The weather causes slippery conditions and increases your braking distance. Drive slowly.

question_text: What must you be aware of?

options.text: - turn on the rear fog lights
- drive at 50 km/h maximum
- drive at 80 km/h maximum

correct_answers.text: - turn on the rear fog lights
- drive at 50 km/h maximum

comment: The fog is so dense here that you cannot see farther than 50 meters. With such a limited view, obstacles and dangerous situations cannot be detected in time when you're driving at high speed. Therefore, you must reduce your speed to a maximum of 50 km/h and drive very carefully. Turn on the rear fog-lamp of your vehicle.

question_text: Why is it necessary to maintain a larger safety distance to the vehicle ahead?

options.text: Because spray water could otherwise impede visibility
Because the braking distance is longer than on a dry road
Because uneven areas of the road will otherwise be detected later

correct_answers.text: Because spray water could otherwise impede visibility
Because the braking distance is longer than on a dry road
Because uneven areas of the road will otherwise be detected later

comment: There is a risk of aquaplaning on wet roads. The braking distance is longer than on dry surfaces. The vehicle in front creates a spray of dirty water that reduces your visibility. Also, you cannot see larger puddles of water in advance. To be able to react well to dangerous situations, keep a greater distance from the vehicle in front and adjust your speed.

question_text: What is the correct course of action in this situation?

options.text: I reduce my speed
I avoid jerky steering movements
I brake hard while in the bend

correct_answers.text: I reduce my speed
I avoid jerky steering movements

comment: Drive carefully, slowly and avoid abrupt steering or braking, because slippery snow or ice can occur at any time.

question_text: While driving, it suddenly begins to rain heavily. What should you do?

options.text: I reduce my speed
I avoid strong acceleration
I reduce the safety distance to the vehicle ahead

correct_answers.text: I reduce my speed
I avoid strong acceleration

comment: Extra care should be taken when driving in heavy rain. This includes adjusting speed, increasing the safe distance and avoiding heavy acceleration, which creates a risk of slipping.
